requirement_text.REQ-049: Variable scoping and merge (instance.zig mergeVariables, EE-09). Merging a key absent from the instance map inserts it with no VARIABLE_OVERWRITTEN event; merging a key already present overwrites it AND produces exactly one VARIABLE_OVERWRITTEN event carrying the key, the old value and the new value -- two explicit tests. Merging an empty map is a no-op producing zero events and leaving the variable map unchanged. Merging a value that a registered variable schema rejects leaves the variable map unchanged, transitions the instance to ERROR (returns {:rejected, unchanged_variables, events}), and produces an EXECUTION_ERROR event -- verified by reading the variable map back and confirming it did not absorb the rejected value. Schema validation goes through REQ-024's validate_payload/3 rather than a second JSON Schema implementation -- verified by inspection (this module doesn't call it directly; the design's caller-composition contract is what satisfies this AC). Variables merged by a task completion are visible to a gateway condition evaluated later in the same completion, demonstrated by an explicit test rather than argued. Also: whole-batch all-or-nothing rejection semantics (REVIEWER-confirmed to match the design) needs its own explicit test.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3. This requirement has real application-executable surface, scope test says YES. Read lib/letflow/design/req049-variable-merge.md and lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex. Write test/specs/REQ-049.md and test code under test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs, following the same convention established by test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs (check its style/structure first). Cover: (1) insert of an absent key, zero events, (2) overwrite of a present key, exactly one VARIABLE_OVERWRITTEN event with key/old/new, (3) empty incoming map -> no-op, zero events, map unchanged (identity), (4) a key flagged {:rejected, failures} in variable_validations -> {:rejected, unchanged_variables, [execution_error_event]}, map genuinely unchanged (read it back), (5) whole-batch all-or-nothing: a batch with both a valid new key and a rejected overwrite key -> neither lands, (6) AC4 (validate_payload/3 reuse) -- since this module doesn't call it directly, verify by inspection/moduledoc reading rather than manufactured busywork, note this explicitly in the spec, (7) AC5 (CEL visibility) -- demonstrate via an explicit test that composes merge/3's output as input to a second read/evaluation step within the same 'completion', proving the returned new_variables map is immediately usable, not deferred.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-049's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one test case that would fail if violated
test/specs/REQ-049.md written explaining each test case's purpose
No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
The whole-batch all-or-nothing rejection semantics has its own explicit test

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-049.md and test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs covering all 5 of REQ-049's acceptance criteria plus the whole-batch all-or-nothing rejection semantics the handoff named explicitly. 20 example tests, no property test (merge/3's branch count is small enough that targeted examples give complete coverage, unlike Transition.transition/3's open-ended input space) -- see the spec's 'Test tier' note. AC1 covered by 4 tests (insert=0 events, overwrite=exactly-1-event with key/old/new, both single- and multi-key). AC2 (empty-map no-op) covered by 2 tests, one asserting map identity (==) not just value equality, per design doc §9's 'no copy divergence' note. AC3 (rejection) covered by 2 tests, verifying by reading the map back per the requirement text's own method, plus the new-key-never-validated carve-out. Whole-batch atomicity gets 3 dedicated tests (new-key-in-rejected-batch, valid-overwrite-in-rejected-batch, first-failure-wins ordering) distinct from the plain AC3 test, as the handoff required. AC4 (validate_payload/3 reuse) is code-inspection only per the design's own resolution (merge/3 never calls it directly) -- re-ran the design doc's own grep recipe myself and found it actually returns 4 matches, all inside doc strings (moduledoc/typedoc prose + the grep command's own quoted example), none in merge/3's or find_rejection/2's real function bodies; documented this discrepancy in the spec as a MINOR design-doc inaccuracy rather than silently reporting a false 'zero matches'. AC5 (CEL visibility) covered by 2 tests demonstrating the merge-then-observe composition contract (including threading merge/3's output into a real Transition.transition/3 call, REQ-044); the full CEL-condition-reads-it half is explicitly flagged as not yet completable until REQ-050 lands (currently a stub), matching the design doc's own forward-dependency note -- not silently claimed as fully closed. No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness. Compiled the test file (ExUnit.start(autorun: false) + Code.require_file, no test execution) to confirm no syntax errors -- did not run mix test, per this role's boundary; that is TEST-RUNNER's job next.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/req049-variable-merge.md §10's grep-based purity verification recipe ('must return zero matches') does not actually return zero matches against the real lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex -- it returns 4 (lines 26, 56, 63, 106), all inside @moduledoc/@typedoc prose describing the caller-composition contract (plus the grep command's own quoted self-reference), not inside merge/3's or find_rejection/2's real function bodies (confirmed by direct read of lines 153-193, zero matches there). Not a purity violation in the implementation -- the design doc's stated verification method just doesn't distinguish prose mentions from real call sites. Documented in test/specs/REQ-049.md's AC4 section rather than silently reported as passing.
